title: Social Signal Bench: Evidence-Weighted Evaluation of Co-occurring Social Signals in Video and Audio
abstract: arXiv:2611.22704v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recognizing social signals such as interest and hesitation requires interpreting context-dependent behaviors that may co-occur in conversation. Existing affective computing benchmarks rarely evaluate such co-occurring signals, and conventional multi-label F1 overlooks semantic relationships and annotator disagreement. We introduce Social Signal Bench, a 47-hour densely annotated benchmark for the evaluation of social signal recognition and engagement, comprising two datasets: Social Signal Bench Video (25 hours), covering ten social signals in audiovisual recordings, and Social Signal Bench Audio (22 hours), covering six signals in audio-only recordings. Each dataset pairs a public training set of online conversational video, of which 10 hours are expert-annotated and the remainder pseudo-labeled, with a private expert-labeled test set spanning four conversational domains. translated_title: 社交信号基准：视频与音频中共现社交信号的证据加权评估
translated_abstract: 识别兴趣和犹豫等社交信号需要解释对话中可能共现的情境依赖行为。现有的情感计算基准很少评估这类共现信号，而传统的多标签F1指标忽略了语义关系和标注者之间的分歧。我们提出了Social Signal Bench，这是一个47小时的密集标注基准，用于评估社交信号识别和参与度，包含两个数据集：Social Signal Bench Video（25小时），涵盖视听记录中的十种社交信号；以及Social Signal Bench Audio（22小时），涵盖纯音频记录中的六种信号。每个数据集将一个公开的在线对话视频训练集（其中10小时由专家标注，其余为伪标签）与一个覆盖四个对话领域的私有专家标注测试集配对。我们还提出了证据加权F1（EW-F1）指标，它对参考（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了Social Signal Bench——一个47小时密集标注的视频与音频社交信号识别基准，并引入证据加权F1（EW-F1）评估指标，以更好地处理共现社交信号、语义关系和标注者分歧问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Social Signal Bench, a 47-hour densely annotated benchmark for social signal recognition in video and audio, along with the Evidence-Weighted F1 (EW-F1) metric to better handle co-occurring signals, semantic relationships, and annotator disagreement.
